leads.name: confbox
leads.note: Multi-format config parser; its TOML entry point is a bundled copy of smol-toml. Counts only as a wrapper path with that family.
leads.family_evidence: confbox 0.3.2 dist/toml.mjs exports parseTOML(text) = stripBOM, then the parse function of dist/_chunks/libs/smol-toml.mjs (14,649 bytes, minified by rolldown, exported as parse/stringify); dist/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md.gz names smol-toml (BSD-3-Clause, squirrelchat/smol-toml) and package.json lists smol-toml ^1.9.1 as a devDependency. The bundle is minified, so a textual diff is impossible; its string literals match smol-toml 1.9.1 dist/ (95 shared; the remaining differences are renamed template-literal variables, escape spelling and the removed ./*.js import paths) and it contains the 1.9.0 option names integersAsBigInt, useLegacyDate, unsafeKeyBehaviour and maxDepth. Its TOML values (TomlDate with isDate/isTime/isLocal) behave like smol-toml's.
leads.control_result: service-config.toml matches the expected typed tree. typed-scalars.toml fails: parseTOML takes no options and calls the bundled parse without integersAsBigInt, so every TOML integer and float is a plain Number and float `exponent = 1e3` comes back as the Number 1000, the same value as integer 1000. Typing Numbers by Number.isInteger gives floats.exponent = {"type": "integer", "value": "1000"}, expected {"type": "float", "value": "1000.0"}. Every other typed-scalars value matches. The documented API cannot tell float 1000.0 from integer 1000.
leads.run: Node v26.10.0 in node@sha256:c8890e48c4572d2f912bf787272b34d122a4009911a5aafe604912194ff89c47 (linux/arm64), npm install confbox@0.3.2

leads.name: toml
leads.note: Registry description claims TOML 1.1.0 compliance for 5.0.1; earlier releases were TOML 0.4.
leads.control_result: service-config.toml matches the expected typed tree. typed-scalars.toml fails: toml.parse returns local date-time, local date and local time values as plain JavaScript strings ('1979-05-27T07:32:00', '1979-05-27', '00:32:00.25'), indistinguishable from TOML strings, so times.local_datetime/local_date/local_time come out as {"type": "string"} instead of datetime-local/date-local/time-local; integers and floats are plain Numbers, so float `exponent = 1e3` is indistinguishable from integer 1000 (observed integer "1000", expected float "1000.0"). The offset date-time is a Date and matches.
leads.run: Node v26.10.0 in node@sha256:c8890e48c4572d2f912bf787272b34d122a4009911a5aafe604912194ff89c47 (linux/arm64), npm install toml@5.0.1

leads.name: @iarna/toml
leads.note: TOML 0.5.0; dates are Date objects with isDate/isTime flags.
leads.control_result: service-config.toml matches the expected typed tree. typed-scalars.toml fails only on floats.exponent: TOML.parse returns integers (within 2^53) and floats as plain Numbers, so float `exponent = 1e3` is the Number 1000 and cannot be told from integer 1000 (observed integer "1000", expected float "1000.0"). Its date objects carry the kinds (FloatingDateTime with isFloating, Date with isDate, Time with isTime) and match.
leads.run: Node v26.10.0 in node@sha256:c8890e48c4572d2f912bf787272b34d122a4009911a5aafe604912194ff89c47 (linux/arm64), npm install @iarna/toml@2.2.5

leads.name: @taplo/lib
leads.api_lead: Taplo.initialize() then taplo.decode(toml: string, parse?: boolean) (TOML to JSON); format and lint are the other documented methods
leads.note: WebAssembly build of the Rust taplo crate (same family as the selected Rust taplo path). It fails the typed-tree controls through its only value API and is also not measurable at parser-source level as published; it is not promoted.
leads.run: Node v26.10.0 in node@sha256:c8890e48c4572d2f912bf787272b34d122a4009911a5aafe604912194ff89c47 (linux/arm64, --network none), the pinned @taplo/lib 0.5.0 tarball (gitHead 48e4c083) unpacked locally; taplo.decode(text, false) on both controls
leads.control_result: Both controls fail the typed tree. decode returns a JSON text in which every TOML date-time is a plain JSON string: service-config owner.since comes back as "1979-05-27T07:32:00Z" and typed-scalars times.offset as "1979-05-27T00:32:00.5-07:00", local_datetime, local_date and local_time as strings, indistinguishable from TOML strings (expected datetime, datetime-local, date-local and time-local). Integers, floats (exponent printed as 1000.0), strings, keys and tables otherwise match. The package declares no other value-tree API (index.d.ts lists format, lint, encode and decode).
leads.runnability_blocker: dist/index.js (35,642,470 bytes) embeds a precompiled WebAssembly build of the Rust taplo crate. V8 JavaScript coverage and the JavaScript AFL++ bridge see only the JS glue; Rust-level coverage would need a rebuild of the wasm module from the taplo repository with a wasm32 coverage runtime that the published package does not contain, so the measured binary would no longer be the pinned release.

leads.name: js-toml
leads.control_result: service-config.toml parses (offset date-time as a TomlDate with kind 'offset-date-time'). typed-scalars.toml fails: load(text) has only a maxDepth option and returns every TOML integer and float as a plain Number, so float `exponent = 1e3` comes back as the Number 1000, the same value as integer 1000 (typed by Number.isInteger it reads as integer "1000", expected float "1000.0"). Its TomlDate kind accessor ('offset-date-time', 'local-date-time', 'local-date') and TomlTime keep the four date-time kinds apart.
leads.run: Node v26.10.0 in node@sha256:c8890e48c4572d2f912bf787272b34d122a4009911a5aafe604912194ff89c47 (linux/arm64), npm install js-toml@2.0.1
